name: Waropen
confidence_why: The only first-hand account, Flassy, Animung and Sawaki's 1994 phonology of Waropen, states that stress is non-contrastive and unpredictable, yet its own word lists mark the second syllable with striking regularity, and Kamholz 2014 relays an undocumented claim by van Velzen 1994 that the language has three tones, so the variable classification rests on a single source that does not fully agree with itself.
catalog_citation: Flassy, Don A.L., Lisidus Animung & Rachel Sawaki. 1994. Fonologi bahasa Waropen. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa, Departemen Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. xi+112 pp.
catalog_locator: Sec. 2.7.1 'Tekanan', p. 39; sec. 2.7.2 'Lagu pada Suku Kata', pp. 39-40; stress-marked word lists by syllable count in ch. 3 secs. 3.2.2-3.2.4, pp. 42-45
catalog_quote: 2.7.1 Tekanan. Pada bahasa Waropen, berdasarkan data yang dikumpulkan, belum ditemukan adanya tekanan pada kata-kata dalam lingkungan yang identik maupun analogis yang fonemik. Pemunculannya pun tidak dapat diramalkan. Tekanan kadang-kadang jatuh pada suku yang pertama, kadang-kadang pada suku yang kedua. Pada kata yang bersuku tiga pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku yang kedua. Kata yang bersuku empat dan lima pada umumnya tekanan jatuh pada suku kata yang ketiga dan yang keempat. Contoh: /'pa ko/ 'beras', /'su si/ 'susu', /fa 'ne/ 'ke belakang', /yi'sira/ 'ia duduk', /yopa 'boyo/ 'dia tidur tertiarap', /yowaya'rawo/ 'dia menyangkal'. [p. 39] ... 3.2.2 ... /o.'ro/ [o.'ro] 'tiga', /a.'ko/ [a.'ko] 'empat', /o.'na/ [o.'na] 'bicara', /a.'do/ [a.'do] 'ikan', /a.'na/ [a.'na] 'tanah', /na.na/ [na.'na] 'perut', /ki.'ro/ [ki.'ro] 'pantat', /na.'no/ [na.'no] 'keringat', /ra.'ra/ [ra.'ra] 'darah', /sa.'si/ [sa.'si] 'susu' ... /kem.'bu/ [kem.'bu] 'lutut' ... /man.'ga/ [maŋ.'ga] 'suami. lelaki', /day.'da/ [dai.'da] 'bapak', /bin.'ga/ [biŋ.'ga] 'perempuan', /nun.'gu/ [nuŋ.'gu] 'manusia' [p. 42] ... 3.2.4 ... /a.'re.na.do/ [a.'re.na.do] 'wajah' ... /ma.'ma.ni.ko/ [ma.'ma.ni.ko] 'rata' ... /ka.'re.si.na/ [ka.'re.si.na] 'rotan' [p. 44]

new_statements.translation: In Waropen, on the basis of the data collected, no stress has been found that is phonemic, in identical or analogous environments. Nor can its occurrence be predicted. Stress sometimes falls on the first syllable, sometimes on the second. In three-syllable words stress generally falls on the second syllable. In four- and five-syllable words stress generally falls on the third and the fourth syllable [respectively]. Examples: /'pako/ 'rice', /'susi/ 'milk', /fa'ne/ 'to the back', /yi'sira/ 'he sits', /yopa'boyo/ 'he sleeps face down', /yowaya'rawo/ 'he denies'.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (125 pp., text present; Internet Archive copy of repositori.kemdikbud.go.id, listed). I rendered p. 51 (printed p. 39) as an image and read it: section 2.7 'Unsur Suprasegmental', 2.7.1 'Tekanan' contains the quoted passage word for word (only line-break hyphens 'be-lum', 'ber-suku' differ), followed by the six examples /'pa ko/, /'su si/, /fa 'ne/, /yi'sira/, /yopa 'boyo/, /yowaya'rawo/. Printed p. 40 (2.7.2) gives pitch contours 3-2 ['pa.ko], 2-3 [fo.'ne], 2-3-2 [yi.'si.ra], 2-3-4-3 [yo.pa.'bo.yo]. the compilers translation is accurate. STATUS: agree, first-hand phonology monograph, openly retrievable. On the identity of the variety: ok. Ch. 1 (the text) says the sample is D…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive (no minimal pairs). The authors call its position unpredictable, but their own generalizations by word length (2nd syllable of 3, 3rd of 4, 4th of 5) all amount to the penultimate syllable, and 5 of their 6 examples are penult-stressed; disyllables vary between initial (= penult: 'pako, 'susi) and final (fa'ne). Provisional reading: non-phonemic stress with a penultimate tendency; the 'fixed: penultimate syllable' label is my inference, not the authors' wording.
new_statements.exceptions: Disyllables may be stressed on either syllable (e.g. /fa'ne/ final vs /'pako/ initial); authors state placement 'tidak dapat diramalkan' (cannot be predicted) and give only 'pada umumnya' (in general) tendencies. Section 2.7.2 adds that stressed syllables carry pitch movement on a 2-4 scale. Note separately Kamholz 2014:95 fn.1 reporting van Velzen's (1994) undocumented claim of three lexical tones in Waropen.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level, isolated citation forms (including inflected verb forms with subject proclitic y- such as yi'sira, yopa'boyo). Data from Sanggei village (Ureifaisei), Waropen Kai dialect.
new_statements.identity_note: Flassy et al. 1994 collected their phonology data in Desa Ureifaisei (kampung Sanggei), Kecamatan Waropen Bawah, i.e. the Waropen Kai dialect (Glottolog waro1243), 'dengan memilih dialek Sanggei'. Held's 1942 grammar and 1956 texts are mainly Nubuai (also Waropen Kai), with some Napan (napa1243) material.

sources.note: Sec. 2.7.1 Tekanan, p. 39: no phonemic stress contrast found; placement 'cannot be predicted' - sometimes 1st, sometimes 2nd syllable; trisyllables generally 2nd syllable; 4- and 5-syllable words generally 3rd and 4th syllable; examples /'pako/, /'susi/, /fa'ne/, /yi'sira/, /yopa'boyo/, /yowaya'rawo/ (5 of 6 penult). Sec. 2.7.2 gives pitch contours (levels 2-4) on the stressed syllables.
